scope: Bounded primary-source review for active observation, yoked passive replay, learning/memory measurement, and static-versus-temporal display controls
execution_policy: Read-only inspection of original papers and publisher/archival records; no implementation, browser run, deployment, external communication, participant recruitment, human study, or causal Gate 9 result.

primary_sources.title: Active manual control of object views facilitates visual recognition
primary_sources.source_type: Primary experimental paper; active exploration with yoked passive replay
claims_used: Active viewers rotated novel 3-D objects; passive viewers saw the exact same image sequence replayed from an active exploration.
The active condition showed more efficient later visual recognition in that object task.
A yoked exact-sequence replay is a relevant way to hold visual content constant while changing control over its presentation.
primary_sources.gate9_use: The watch condition must receive the chooser's realized baseline and exactly two query occurrences in the same order, with source-card IDs, occurrence indices, duplicates, and terminal hash preserved.
primary_sources.limits: The task used manually rotated virtual objects and an object-recognition outcome. Motor/efference cues, action timing, selected views, and object-specific strategies remain possible contributors; the result does not establish an agency mechanism or a Gate 9 performance effect.

primary_sources.title: Deconstructing the effect of self-directed study on episodic memory
primary_sources.source_type: Primary experimental paper; four self-directed versus passive/yoked memory experiments
claims_used: Across four experiments, self-directed study improved recognition relative to passive observation.
The advantage persisted when control was reduced to pressing a button when ready to advance, implicating timing/attentional coordination rather than only content selection.
Yoked designs can match study content while leaving episode timing, attention, revisitation, and other exposure details different.
primary_sources.gate9_use: Freeze practice, item/order/duplicate rules, exposure duration, stopping, submission, and terminal conditions before any human use; treat the chooser's realized sequence as the watch route and retain the static route's reinspection affordance as an explicit condition difference.
primary_sources.limits: The experiments used spatial object arrays and recognition/spatial memory outcomes. They do not validate the finite 5-D world model, establish a benefit of agency in this task, or supply a participant-free causal result.

primary_sources.title: Learning the Concept of Function With Dynamic Visualizations
primary_sources.source_type: Primary experimental paper; static, linear dynamic, and interactive dynamic presentations
claims_used: 157 students learned with static, linear dynamic, or interactive dynamic representations while core task content was held constant.
Dynamic groups outperformed the static group in the reported immediate posttest; linear and interactive dynamic groups did not differ significantly.
Static representations permit repeated inspection, while linear dynamic presentation exposes temporal change transiently and imposes different integration demands.
primary_sources.gate9_use: Treat terminal information matching as separate from temporal access, memory load, reinspection, agency, and pixel parity; use the paper as a control warning rather than as a prediction for the finite point-world benchmark.
primary_sources.limits: This was a 25-minute mathematics lesson with 14-year-old students and an immediate posttest, with no actor-to-observer yoked replay. Static/dynamic conditions may differ in temporal information and instructional scaffolding, so the result cannot be transferred to Gate 9 or interpreted as a general static-versus-watch effect.

derived_gate9_requirements.design: Let the chooser's two finite query occurrences define the watched stream. Preserve the same baseline, query labels, order, occurrence count, duplicates, source-card IDs, and terminal information hash; reject any substituted or independently selected watch sequence.
derived_gate9_requirements.status: Application instrument rule; not a human outcome.

derived_gate9_requirements.design: Freeze practice, per-card exposure/viewing windows, stopping, submission, and terminal display rules. Record timing and attention as condition variables because content matching alone does not match study experience.
derived_gate9_requirements.status: Application control rule; no causal claim without approved participants and observed data.

derived_gate9_requirements.design: Use identical cards and preserve duplicate/order records in the static sheet. Report all-card simultaneous access and reinspection as intended affordances; compare only terminal raw-record equality as information parity.
derived_gate9_requirements.status: Application reporting rule; the paper does not validate this instrument.

limits: No source establishes that the Looking Glass Gate 9 instrument is correct, understandable, useful, or causally effective.
No participants or human outcomes are present in this source pass; software route checks cannot stand in for learning or memory observations.
Terminal exact information matching does not imply matched temporal exposure, attention, agency, motor experience, memory trace, or pixels.
The cited studies are heterogeneous primary experiments and should not be pooled into an effect estimate for the finite 5-D point-world task.
